Conversion of an efp fit to a gam fit for plotting

Source: R/as.gam.R
as.gam.Rd

Converts an efp fit to a gam object, so that the plotting and prediction tools in the mgcv package can be used. The coefficients and their variances are those estimated by efp, but the smoothing parameters and effective degrees of freedom in the gam object are not.

Usage

as.gam(object)

Arguments

object

an efp fitted model

Value

an object of class gam, see gamObject

Details

The conversion fits a model using mgcv, which can take a very long time if the model has many random effects. Predictions do not need the conversion, see predict.efp.

Examples

data(ef_data)
ef_data$sampleID <- factor(paste(ef_data$date, ef_data$siteID,
                                 ef_data$lifestage, ef_data$species))
m1 <- efp(count ~ lifestage + s(doy, k = 3),
          data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID)

m1_gam <- as.gam(m1)
#> Note that, although predictions and plots will be correct
#>  the smoothing parameters and degrees of freedom in the gam object are not those estimated by efp!
plot(m1_gam)
